item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong evidence that Kishida could mobilize formal institutions, budgets, expert panels, the Diet, and alliance/security channels.\nI did not find equally strong evidence of deep personal control over appointments or a disciplined loyalist machine; most mobilization appears institutional and coalition-based.\nThe clearest negative evidence is political fragility: scandal, low approval, and compromise with conservative blocs, not a total failure to mobilize the state.","evidence":[{"title":"Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-01-30","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html","summary":"Kishida explicitly asked the Diet to turn the year’s priorities into concrete action, tying the agenda to wage growth, child support, disaster response, fiscal reform, digital administration, labor reform, and defense buildup. This is direct evidence of mobilizing the cabinet and bureaucracy toward the chosen program.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2","8B.3"]},{"title":"Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-06-21","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida said the reform headquarters had pushed core political-funding measures, the law had been amended, and the next steps were a third-party inspections-and-audits body plus lower disclosure thresholds. That shows actual institutional mobilization, not just rhetoric.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.3"]},{"title":"Liaison Meeting of the Government and Ruling Parties","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-07-03","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/03sei_yoto.html","summary":"Kishida reported that nearly all bills and treaties passed, including the Political Funds Control Act, child-care support, and food/agriculture legislation, and he credited the government-ruling-party coalition. This shows practical mobilization of regulators, local authorities, and safety planning for a policy objective.","question_ids":["8B.2","8B.3"]},{"title":"Statement by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio upon the General Resignation of the Kishida Cabinet","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-10-01","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202410/1001danwa.html","summary":"Kishida summarized his term as economic revival, defense strengthening, and political reform, and said the cabinet had worked to restore accountability after the fundraising scandal. That is mixed evidence: coalition bargaining helped him mobilize power, but it also indicates dependence on bloc management rather than purely programmatic control.","question_ids":["8B.3","8B.1"]},{"title":"Japan’s PM says LDP race should be transparent and he will step aside","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office of Japan","date":"2024-08-14","url":"https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html","summary":"Kishida’s own exit statement shows he chose transparent succession and withdrawal rather than attempting to retain office. This is not negative in a democratic sense, but it does mark the limits of his personal mobilization power by late 2024.","question_ids":["8B.3","8B.1"]}]}
